title: Retail Sales Performance Report, 2023-2024
executive_summary: Total 2023-2024 revenue was $445,325.07 across 520 orders, an average of $856.39 per order. Revenue grew 10.08% year over year, from $211,976.28 in 2023 to $233,348.79 in 2024, with 2024 momentum peaking in Q3. The East region leads regional sales, order values are highly skewed toward a small number of large orders, and customer concentration is low: the single largest customer accounts for just 6.24% of revenue.

key_findings.statement: Overall performance: the cleaned 2023-2024 data shows total revenue of $445,325.07 across 520 orders, giving an average order value of $856.39.
Regional comparison: the East leads with $130,516.68 in revenue, followed by the North ($124,845.75), the West ($99,428.16) and the South ($90,534.48); the East outperforms the South by $39,982.20.
2024 quarterly trend: revenue built through the year, from $36,108.32 in Q1 to $56,616.79 in Q2, peaking at $71,674.98 in Q3 before easing to $68,948.70 in Q4; Q3 exceeded Q1 by $35,566.66.
Year-over-year change: revenue increased from $211,976.28 in 2023 to $233,348.79 in 2024, a rise of 10.08%, equivalent to $21,372.51 in additional revenue.
High-discount electronics: 22 electronics orders carried a discount of 20% or more, generating $50,035.32 in revenue, about 11.24% of total revenue.

Order revenue distribution: revenue per order is highly right-skewed, with a mean of $856.39 roughly 2.73 times the median of $313.28, a standard deviation of $1,295.74, and values spanning $5.27 to $7,844.02.
Customer concentration: the base is broad, with 222 unique customers, and reliance on any single account is limited; the top customer contributed $27,793.12, or 6.24% of total revenue.

limitations: The data covers only 2023-2024, so longer-term trends and seasonality cannot be assessed; in particular, the Q3-to-Q4 2024 dip cannot be attributed to a cause.
Figures reflect order revenue only; returns, cancellations, costs and margins are not captured, so high-discount electronics revenue does not indicate profitability.
The analysis is descriptive; no statistical significance tests were run on regional or year-over-year differences.
Customer concentration is summarised by the top customer alone; a broader view (e.g., top-10 share) is not available in these findings.
conclusion: The business is growing, with revenue up 10.08% in 2024 and momentum concentrated in the second half of the year. The East and North regions drive the majority of sales, while the South lags. Revenue depends on a small number of large orders rather than any single customer, suggesting opportunity in growing mid-sized orders and in reviewing the margin impact of deep electronics discounts.
